lines: How do you encourage your friends who are trying to change their behavior?
Suppose you see a friend who has been working on a diet and losing a lot of weight.
Definitely, you would want to tell her that she looks great.
Anyone who hears positive comments will feel good, and this feedback will also be very encouraging.
However, if you end the discussion there, the only feedback your friend is getting is about the outcome.
Instead, continue the discussion by asking about the process.
Ask her what she is doing to be so successful.
When the conversation focuses on the process of change rather than the outcome, it encourages her to keep making the change.
body.text: How do you encourage your friends who are trying to change their behavior? Suppose you see a friend who has been working on a diet and losing a lot of weight. Definitely, you would want to tell her that she looks great. Anyone who hears positive comments will feel good, and this feedback will also be very encouraging. However, if you end the discussion there, the only feedback your friend is getting is about the outcome. Instead, continue the discussion by asking about the process. Ask her what she is doing to be so successful. What is she eating? Where is she working out? When the conversation focuses on the process of change rather than the outcome, it encourages her to keep making the change.
